html:
A total eclipse of the Sun on 28 May 585 BCE that, according to Herodotus, was foretold by Thales of Miletus. If the story is true, it is the earliest eclipse known to have been predicted in advance.

Herodotus says that Lydia and the Medes had been at war for five years. In the sixth year, during a battle, day suddenly turned into night. Both armies stopped fighting and made peace. The deal was sealed with a marriage between the families of the two kings, Alyattes of Lydia and Cyaxares of Media, and the Halys River became the border.

Modern astronomers can date the eclipse exactly. Whether Thales could really predict it is doubtful: he may have heard of eclipse cycles from Babylonian astronomers, but they could not say where an eclipse would be seen. The story mattered anyway. It made Thales the model of the wise man who reads nature, and it gives one of the earliest fixed dates in Greek history.
sum: A total eclipse of the Sun on 28 May 585 BCE that, according to Herodotus, was foretold by Thales of Miletus. If the story is true, it is the earliest eclipse known to have been predicted in advance.
